newsitem.title: INDIA: Toyota India project to cost $340mln -PTI.
newsitem.headline: Toyota India project to cost $340mln -PTI.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp will invest nearly $240 million of a total of $340 million in its joint venture to manufacture light commercial vehicles with India's Kirloskar group, the Press Trust of India said on Sunday.

The news agency quoted Vikram Kirloskar, a leading executive of the Kirloskar group, as saying that Toyota will hold 70 percent and the Indian group 30 percent in the project to be funded entirely by equity capital.
He said the joint venture was expected to be launched on July 24. The first vehicle is expected to roll out in 1999.

PTI named the 10-seater Kijang sports utility vehicle with a 1,500 cc diesel engine as the first product to be launched by the company. The annual production capacity is expected to be between 20,000 and 30,000 vehicles.
On Friday, Toyota executive vice-president Akira Yokoi told Reuters in Tokyo that they hoped to announce the joint venture agreement before the start of summer holidays in Japan on August 9.
"We are putting finishing touches to the details before making an application (to the Indian government for the joint venture)," he said.
Yokoi said Bangalore was one of four possible sites for the venture. PTI said Bangalore was the likely choice.
